problem: If $cot⁡x=\sqrt{2}$ for some $x,$ then find the value of $cot⁡(x-9\pi ).$
worked_solution:
The period of $y=cot⁡x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for any integer $n,$ we have

$$
cot⁡x=cot⁡(x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-9$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡x & =cot⁡(x+(-9)\cdot \pi ) \\  & =cot⁡(x-9\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $cot⁡x=\sqrt{2},$ then $cot⁡(x-9\pi )=\sqrt{2}.$
